text:
sara: Quick heads-up — new model drop: LlamaX-13B-v2 (q4_0) landed in the intake bucket. Need to decide prioritization for bring-up, plus a concrete chat template + tool-contract to validate structured outputs before we promote to Dedicated. Quick notes: perf looks on-par with baseline on latency, but eval-bench shows a small slot-fill regression on the FAQ and KB-responder tests. Who can take ownership?

kevin: I can own the initial QA/priority triage this week. Can you paste the basic perf + regression numbers?

sara: TL;DR from eval run (run id: 2026-03-18-llx13b-v2):
- throughput median latency: 48ms/token (baseline 50ms)
- p95 latency: 210ms (baseline 220ms)
- slot-fill F1 dropped 3.9% absolute on KB-responder suite (critical)
- hallucination score (synthetic QA): +2.1% false assertions

eval-bot: automated summary: "priority: medium-high; risk: slot-fill regressions + hallucination drift; recommend targeted prompt + eval set before rollout."

anika: thanks. propose we follow the usual lightweight bring-up checklist but add explicit tool-calling contract tests for these flows. draft checklist: 
1) Smoke perf & memory on dedicated instance
2) Run regression eval against production prompts (sampling + few-shot variants)
3) Run structured-output schema tests for all tools (see sample below)
4) Quantization sanity: run 8-bit/4-bit variants and compare generation errors
5) Canary rollout with fallback to baseline model

lee: +1. For step 3, we need a canonical chat template that all integrators use so the model sees the same framing. Suggest this chat skeleton: 

```
System: You are a helpful assistant that answers customer KB queries. Always return a JSON object exactly matching the schema in the "response_schema" field. Never output free text outside the JSON.
User: {"query": "<user question>", "context": "<kb-snippet>"}
Assistant: <MODEL_GENERATION_JSON>
```

lee: And the schema we run tests against (contract):
```
{
  "response_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "answer": {"type": "string"},
      "sources": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
      "confidence": {"type": "number"}
    },
    "required": ["answer", "sources", "confidence"]
  }
}
```

kevin: Nice. We'll need both soft-fail and hard-fail expectations: e.g., confidence >= 0.3 for auto-fulfillment; JSON parseable w/o heuristics for hard pass. Add metrics: schema-parse rate, required-field completeness, avg confidence.

sara: Agreed. Also include an example tool-call pattern for our router/tooling tests — this is what integrators send to the API (we'll use as canonical test input):

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "llamaX-13b-v2-q4",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a KB assistant. Return ONLY JSON following the response_schema."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "\n{\"query\": \"How do I rotate API keys?\", \"context\": \"...kb snippet...\"}\n"}
  ],
  "stream": false,
  "max_tokens": 256
}
```

anika: For quantization experiments, note the flags we used in this run: `--q-type q4_0 --act-ordering=default --kv-compress=false`. When we test q4_1 and q8, we should track slot-fill delta vs fp16 baseline and also token-level perplexity on heldout prompts.

eval-bot: additional metrics from last automated run:
- schema-parse-rate: 91.2%
- required-fields-complete: 94.1%
- avg-confidence: 0.58
- hallucination-inserts-per-1000: 12 (baseline 9)

lee: That hallucination bump explains the F1 drop. Hypothesis: quantized attention kernels slightly change token sampling near entity boundaries. We should run focused prompts that exercise entity extraction & attribution.

kevin: Proposal for prioritization:
- Priority A (this sprint): fix gated KB responder flows + schema failures >= 5%
- Priority B: wider canary rollouts (if A meets targets)
- Priority C: auto-promote to Dedicated only after 2 consecutive daily runs meeting thresholds

sara: Thresholds proposed: schema-parse-rate >= 98%, required-fields-complete >= 99%, slot-fill F1 within 1% of baseline, hallucination-inserts <= baseline + 1.

anika: I'll kick off q4_1 and q8 experiments today and post results to this thread. cc @kevin for prioritization decisions.

kevin: Great. One more practical: add a short eval harness snippet for others to reproduce locally. Put this in the repo under `eval/llmx_onboard.sh`. Example here: 
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
python eval/run_contract_tests.py \
  --model llamaX-13b-v2-q4 \
  --prompts eval/prompts/kb_queries.jsonl \
  --schema eval/schemas/kb_schema.json \
  --output reports/llmx_v2_run.json
```

sara: Perfect. I'll schedule a 30m sync on Thursday to review numbers and decide canary window. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

lee: tagging checklist owner: @kevin for triage, @anika for quant tests, I can own schema tests.

eval-bot: note: run artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/llmx/1851122334/

kevin: I'll update the prioritization board and ping product if we need accelerated Dedicated capacity.

sara: ✅ closing loop — please drop quick status updates in this thread when runs finish.
